waistPercent.note: How much narrower the middle is than a straight wrap. 0 = straight wrap. With Print-ready on, it is lowered automatically so the walls never overhang more than 45°.

voxelSizeMm.note: Grid used to draw the bridge surface. Smaller = smoother and more exact, but slower. Made coarser automatically on big parts.

voxelSize.note: Smallest voxel the design space may use. The first pass voxel comes from the voxel budget; the Normal and Fine levels use Voxel target size.

designSpace.note: How far the connector may wander from the straight path, as a fraction of the gap between the surfaces.

analysisVoxelBudget.note: Maximum voxels in the design space. Fewer = much faster.

refinement.note: Draft = design + clearance on the first-pass voxel (about 1.5 mm). Normal and Fine refine the Draft on a finer voxel: Fine uses the voxel target size, Normal is halfway between Draft and the target. A level unlocks when the one before it has finished.

voxelTarget.note: Voxel size of the Fine level. Smaller = more detail, much slower. Normal is halfway between the Draft voxel and this size.

volumeFraction.note: Material amount: share of the design space that may be filled. Left = light, right = strong. The weight next to it is an estimate for the first pass.

printReady.note: Print-ready (test): printed with the flange face on the bed. Nothing grows below the bed, and every voxel must rest on voxels below it (45° overhang at most), so there are no supports and no floating islands. Method: additive manufacturing filter (Langelaar 2017).

material.label: PLA
material.note: Used only for the weight and sag readout (solid, 100% infill). Printed parts are weaker across layers.

maxSagMm.note: A sag above this (or a solver result that is not a valid number) is treated as a failed solve: the panel shows a warning instead of the number.

cantileverRatio.note: Self-test: the solver's cantilever tip drop divided by beam theory must fall in this range.

filterRadius.note: In voxels. Bigger = thicker, smoother members.

maxIterations.note: The design stops earlier when it stops changing.

payloadMassKg.note: Mass of the tool and what it carries.

accelFactor.note: Multiplier for robot motion (1 = standing still).

extraForceN.note: Optional extra force at the centre of mass of the tool.

faceExtrudeMm.note: Gap: how far a red face is pushed outward. Nothing can grow inside this zone. 0 = only the face itself.

robotOffsetMm.note: Keep-out cylinder below the robot side: plate diameter plus this offset on each side. Nothing grows inside it.

objectGrowMm.note: Gap: how far a red object is offset (grown evenly in all directions). 0 = only the object itself.

options.label: Slot (runs outward from the flange centre)

slotLengthMm.note: How far the slot runs outward from each screw, away from the flange centre. Keeps inner screws reachable.

diameterAdjustMm.note: Added to the head clearance diameter of the robot side (Allen head + 0.25).

lengthAdjustMm.note: Added to the head diameter of the robot side. Counted from the top face of the tool start.

voxelBudget.note: Maximum voxels in the refined grid. If it would be more, the refined voxel is made coarser automatically.

bandVoxels.note: How far (in analysis voxels) the refined design may grow around the existing material.

maxIterations.note: The refined design stops earlier when it stops changing.

stiffnessTolerance.note: The refined design may lose this share of stiffness (compared with the coarse design) in exchange for less material.

shrinkStep.note: Share of the material cap removed per shrink round.

minVolumeFraction.note: The material may not drop below this share of the coarse volume.

passes.note: Smoothing passes per click (each pass blurs the shape by about one voxel). More = rounder, but thin members get thinner. The volume is kept.

solver.note: Topology optimization (SIMP) and its stiffness solver. Change only with the solver self-test (Advanced mode, Run solver self-test).

multigrid.note: Multigrid preconditioner (Amir, Aage & Lazarov 2014): far fewer solver steps on big grids. damping = Jacobi factor × largest eigenvalue. pivotDrop = a coarsest-level pivot smaller than this × its diagonal is dropped (no stiffness there; stops Inf / NaN). enabled false = the old Jacobi preconditioner.
